correctness.rationale: All six ordered pivot histories are accounted for. The conditional second-pivot probability cancels the corresponding 2-by-2 principal minor against the Schur-complement error, yielding E_2=(2det A/tr A) sum_i 1/t_i with t_i=tr A-(A^2)_ii/A_ii. Substituting K=I+(L-1)vv* gives an exact concave separable function of w_i=|v_i|^2. Strict Jensen and simplex extremal arguments prove both extrema, uniqueness, and limiting ratio; one-step identity and n=2 recovery prove minimality. Standalone verifier exactly enumerates complete finite histories on rational test matrices. Finite checks are corroboration, not a global proof.

limitations: Only L>1 and the 3-by-3 positive-definite one-spike spectral family; exact sequential RPCholesky after precisely two pivots.
Does not address other eigenvalue multiplicities, large dimensions, finite precision, or nonadaptive/blocked pivot rules.
Self-review only; independent validation not performed.

originality.rationale: The original RPCholesky algorithm, one-step nonlinear expected-residual map, general contraction bounds, and known DPP expected-error formula are credited. The new statement is the exact actual two-step orientation law and complete sharp extrema at fixed spectrum {L,1,1}; prior theory does not state those extrema or imply them via its general upper bounds without a new nontrivial Schur-complement calculation and concavity argument. Actual semantic searches and targeted primary full-text sections did not locate a covering statement. Residual risk remains, and independent priority verification is absent.
residual_risks: A prior specialized Schur-complement or subset-sampling calculation could have characterized precisely the same 3-by-3 spike orientation extrema under another name.

value.rationale: RPCholesky trace error is the central approximation measure in its motivating paper. This classification isolates its first possible coordinate-orientation sensitivity despite fixed spectrum, fully determines the best/worst basis and their 50% asymptotic gap, and distinguishes adaptive sampling from 2-DPP. The specific finite model is natural (smallest possible dimension, rank-one spike) and isolates a performance control variable that spectral-tail bounds cannot detect.
